correctness.rationale: The exact finite lower bounds n=5..9 follow from published gp(P2 square C_n)=4 and diameter <=5; n=3,4 require at least two by existence of a three-vertex geodesic. The n>=10 lower bound is supplied by an explicit complete 88-node canonical-label search for a three-coloring of the isometric P5 square K2 strip. No timeouts/pruning assertions are used. Complete witnesses for 15 base orders are checked against reconstructed BFS geodesics. Six-column locality holds because n>=10 makes every six-column strip isometric and every at-most-five-edge geodesic project into it. Ten-column periodic prefixes of base orders 12,14,15,21 supply an admissible length-four closed state walk, whose repetition yields every larger circumference modulo four. All residue gaps 10,11,13,17 are covered by explicit seeds. Code, data and logs accompany proof; no unsupported infinite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The object and fixed-parameter coloring invariant are defined in arXiv:2601.04351; its statements do not classify circular prisms. The earlier gp-coloring paper implies small-order lower bounds but cannot imply a four-color bounded-distance tail because gp and chi^3_5 differ once diameter exceeds five. Other inspected maximal-set and local-coloring results concern different optimization objectives. Prior same-topic straight-ladder result concerns P_n square P2, not cyclic closure and exceptional n=9. No covering exact formula identified after statement- and parameter-level checks.
